# Amazon MSK

Store provisioned Standard cluster configuration, monitoring settings and tags without a Kafka runtime.

**Status: implemented subset.** Operation selection does not imply complete input or behavior parity.

| Contract | Current implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Service ID | `kafka` |
| Signing name | `kafka` |
| Wire protocol | REST JSON |
| API version | `2018-11-14` |
| Scope | Account and region |
| Execution | Configuration records only |
| Selected operations | 8 of 64 in the pinned model |

## Implemented behavior

See the [implemented feature catalogue](catalogue.md#amazon-msk) for this service's capabilities.

## Limitations and future work

- No brokers, listeners, containers, endpoints, DNS, nodes, bootstrap strings, topics, producer/consumer traffic, runtime state or asynchronous cluster-operation ARN.
- No serverless/V2, configurations/revisions, SCRAM/credentials, auth/encryption/KMS/IAM enforcement, logging/open monitoring, tiered storage, networking allocation or metrics delivery; excluded fields reject even false/null/empty.
- Finite versions/instances/Regions and explicit groups/storage are local boundaries; no changing latest version or default VPC/group/storage inference. NumberOfBrokerNodes follows the pinned 1-15 model, not larger current AWS quotas.
- CloudFormation version/count/instance/storage mutations and explicit immutable-choice removals fail before writing; mutable optional monitoring removal restores DEFAULT. No Terraform runtime waiter or dedicated mutation console.
- The [records guide](../guides/msk-records.md) lists every selected member, nested constraint, default, tag/revision/network/CF boundary and executable lifecycle; remaining APIs and runtime are [future scope](../roadmap/services/msk-runtime.md).

These gaps describe current boundaries and possible follow-up slices. The [roadmap](../roadmap/index.md)
separates proposed work from registered functionality; there are no promised release dates.

## Supported operations

The table is generated from the profile and pinned Smithy model. Routes show REST bindings or the standard
JSON/Query endpoint. RPC v2 CBOR uses its service/operation route, as described in
[protocol handling](../architecture/request-flow.md). Supported members are selected separately in the
[shape whitelist](https://github.com/amjadjibon/tinystack/blob/main/generator/model/profile.json); an enabled operation may reject unsupported options.

| Operation | HTTP binding |
| --- | --- |
| `CreateCluster` | `POST /v1/clusters` |
| `DeleteCluster` | `DELETE /v1/clusters/{ClusterArn}` |
| `DescribeCluster` | `GET /v1/clusters/{ClusterArn}` |
| `ListClusters` | `GET /v1/clusters` |
| `ListTagsForResource` | `GET /v1/tags/{ResourceArn}` |
| `TagResource` | `POST /v1/tags/{ResourceArn}` |
| `UntagResource` | `DELETE /v1/tags/{ResourceArn}` |
| `UpdateMonitoring` | `PUT /v1/clusters/{ClusterArn}/monitoring` |
